cards.text: Nehemiah, governor of Judah, is telling this one himself. His enemies Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem the Arab and the rest hear that the wall is rebuilt, with not one gap left. The doors aren't hung in the gates yet, but friend, that wall is UP.

cards.question: Sanballat and Geshem send Nehemiah a message. Where do they want to meet him?

answers.text: In a village on the plain of Ono
In the royal palace at Susa

cards.question: Sanballat and Geshem have no plans to harm Nehemiah.

cards.text: Nehemiah doesn't go. He sends messengers back with an answer instead.

cards.question: What reason does Nehemiah give Sanballat and Geshem for not coming to the meeting?

answers.text: He's doing a great work and can't stop
He's too sick to make the long trip
The road down to Ono isn't safe

cards.text: He says, "I am doing a great work and cannot come down." Friend, that's the greatest "can't talk, I've got a batch in the oven" of ALL TIME.
They send the same message FOUR times, friend. I've had oven timers give up sooner than these guys.

cards.question: Four times the same invite comes, and each time Nehemiah sends back the ___ reply.

cards.text: The fifth time, Sanballat sends the same message with his young servant. And this time the servant has a letter in his hand.

cards.question: The letter Sanballat's servant carries is sealed.

cards.text: The letter says it's reported among the nations that Nehemiah and the Jews are up to something, and Geshem agrees. GESHEM, friend, the same guy who's been sending the invites!

cards.question: Sanballat's letter claims the Jews are building the wall for a reason. What is it?
Sanballat's letter says that, according to these reports, Nehemiah is going to become their ___.

cards.text: The letter even says he's appointed prophets in Jerusalem to proclaim, 'There is a king in Judah.' Then it warns that soon these rumors will reach the king, so come on, let's talk.

cards.question: Nehemiah writes back to Sanballat. Where does he say these rumors really came from?

cards.text: He says, "There is nothing to these rumors you are spreading; you are inventing them in your own mind." I bet Sanballat did NOT see that reply coming.

cards.question: Nehemiah says the point of all these messages is to help the work get finished.
Nehemiah's enemies say the Jews' hands will be weakened in the work. What does Nehemiah pray?

answers.text: That God would strengthen his hands
That God would weaken their hands
That God would finish the work

cards.text: Later, Nehemiah goes to the house of Shemaiah son of Delaiah, a man who is confined to his house.
Shemaiah warns that they're coming to kill Nehemiah by night, and he wants to meet. Friend, everybody in this chapter wants a MEETING!

cards.question: Shemaiah wants to meet Nehemiah and shut the doors behind them. Where?

answers.text: Out on the plain of Ono

cards.question: Nehemiah agrees to hide in the temple to save his life.

cards.text: Nehemiah says, "Should a man like me run away?" Friend, a stamper like me would already be in that temple with the doors shut and a chair shoved against them.

cards.question: Nehemiah realizes God didn't send Shemaiah. So why did Shemaiah give that prophecy?

cards.text: So that scary warning was bought and paid for. Shemaiah was hired to intimidate Nehemiah into doing what he suggested.

cards.question: If Nehemiah had hidden in the temple, what did his enemies hope would come of it?

answers.text: He would sin and get a bad name
He would be trapped and arrested
He would miss the work on the gates

cards.text: Nehemiah hands it to God: "O my God, remember Tobiah and Sanballat for what they have done." He names Noadiah the prophetess too, and the other prophets who tried to intimidate him.

cards.question: Through every plot, the work goes on. The wall is completed in ___ days, on the twenty-fifth of Elul.

cards.text: FIFTY-TWO DAYS for a whole city wall. Friend, I couldn't get myself out of a junk drawer in fifty-two days, and it took me YEARS.

cards.question: When the enemies hear the wall is done, all the surrounding nations are ___ and ___.
Why does the finished wall leave the surrounding nations feeling that way?

answers.text: They hear the king approves it

cards.text: Meanwhile, back in Judah, the mail is BUSY. The nobles of Judah send Tobiah many letters, and Tobiah's letters keep coming back to them.

cards.question: Many in Judah are bound by oath to Tobiah. What ties them to him?

cards.text: Tobiah is the son-in-law of Shecaniah son of Arah. And his son Jehohanan married the daughter of Meshullam son of Berechiah.

cards.question: The nobles of Judah keep telling Nehemiah about Tobiah's good deeds.
The nobles pass Nehemiah's words along to Tobiah. And what does Tobiah keep sending Nehemiah?

answers.text: Workers to help on the wall

cards.text: The wall is up, but Tobiah's letters keep coming. That's where we'll leave it for now, friend, because Nehemiah's story isn't done yet.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 9 quotes "O my God, remember Tobiah and Sanballat for what they have done.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card calls Nehemiah 'governor of Judah.' That fact comes from Nehemiah 5:14, outside the passage, but the card gives no reference for it. The card cites only Nehemiah 6:1.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'The road down to Ono isn't safe' can be argued as right. Card 3 has just established that Sanballat and Geshem plan to harm Nehemiah (6:2), so the meeting really is unsafe.

rule.text: A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: This story card only repeats verse 3, which card 5 just asked and answered, and adds a joke. It doesn't move the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: This story card only repeats verse 8, which card 15 just asked and answered, and adds a weak reaction line. It is a recap card and doesn't move the passage forward.

No card ever tells the baker what verse 9 says the messages were for: 'they were all trying to frighten us.' Intimidation is the thread of the whole chapter (6:9, 13, 14, 19). This true or false card only asks the baker to reject a straw statement, so the real purpose is never learned.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'That God would finish the work' can be argued as right. Asking God to strengthen his hands is a prayer for the work to get done, and 6:16 says the task was accomplished by God.

rule.text: A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'He would miss the work on the gates' can be argued as right. Verse 9 says the enemies wanted the work never finished, and stop 1 built the whole plot around pulling Nehemiah away from the work.

rule.text: A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The joke 'I couldn't get myself out of a junk drawer in fifty-two days, and it took me YEARS' says Papa Dorin eventually got himself out. That contradicts his backstory: he was called out by the angel. The comparison also doesn't match the core action. The verse is about finishing a big job fast, and the joke is about being stuck and rescued.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The 'story isn't over' line nearly copies the doc's example: 'That's where we'll leave it for now, friend' versus 'And that's where we'll leave it for now. Trust me, friend.'

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates stop 2, with 6 of 10 choice cards. There are only 2 true or false cards and 2 fill in the blank cards. Both stops also open their choice cards with the same multiple choice, then true or false sequence.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
